item.title: Norikura Highland: An Alpine Plateau of Meadows and Waterfalls — Guide
item.description: Norikura Highland (Norikura Kogen) is a scenic alpine plateau at the foot of 3,026-metre Mount Norikura, offering cool highland scenery of marshland boardwalk trails, waterfalls, ponds and alpine meadows that bloom with wildflowers in summer and colour in autumn. Private cars are banned on the mountain road to protect the environment, but a bus climbs to Tatamidaira at over 2,700 metres, near the summit, giving relatively easy access to some of Japan’s highest road-reachable alpine scenery, with short walks to viewpoints and, for the prepared, a hike to the peak.

item.title: Nishizawa Valley: A Waterfall Hiking Trail Through Pristine Nature — Guide
item.description: Nishizawa Valley offers one of Yamanashi’s most rewarding half-day hikes, a loop trail that follows a clear mountain river through pristine forest past a series of waterfalls, culminating in the Nanatsugama Godan-no-taki, a beautiful tiered cascade of pools and falls counted among Japan’s 100 most celebrated waterfalls. The valley is especially popular in autumn when the foliage peaks, and the well-maintained trail combines genuine natural beauty with a manageable half-day of walking suited to reasonably fit visitors.

item.title: Oirase Stream: Aomori's Most Beautiful Forest Walk — Guide
item.description: The Oirase Stream is a designated National Scenic Treasure — 14 km of pristine forest gorge threaded by a rushing mountain stream and dotted with named waterfalls. The trail between Yakeyama and Nenokuchi is one of Japan’s most celebrated nature walks, reaching its peak in late-October foliage. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Towada-Hachimantai NP, Aomori Hours Trail always open (daylight best) Admission Free Time needed 2–4 hours (walk sections) Best time Late Oct–early Nov (autumn); fresh green in June What to See The Choshi Otaki and Kumoi falls among 14 named cascades.

item.title: Nikko Nature: Kegon Falls, Lake Chuzenji & Okunikko
item.description: Tochigi’s natural landscape is dominated by the mountains and waterways of Nikko National Park. Within a 30-kilometre arc north of Nikko town, the terrain rises from cedar forest through alpine lake shoreline to open highland marshland and active volcanic ridges. The concentration of natural features — waterfalls, caldera lake, wetland plateau, gorge — within a single day-trip area from Tokyo is unusual even by Japanese standards. This guide covers the main natural destinations in order of access from Nikko town, with practical details on transport, access costs, and the best times to visit each.
